scoring: score = 0.4*demand + 0.3*2D feasibility + 0.3*originality (1-5 each); list order is the final editorial rank, which also weighs kit reuse and fit with the explainer pilot

formats.short_9x16_70-80s: vertical TikTok/Shorts, man_ia_c 'N seconds' template: title card, countdown HUD, serif italic captions, 5-8 beats, end card with a real fact + 'which next?' CTA
formats.long_16x9_8-12min: 16:9 YouTube, Awaken/IFOLOGY template: 'you' cold open (0:00-0:30), 'here's how it works' science, escalating timeline or stakes, options/verdict, payoff; 9:16 60-90s cut-down from the cold open

originality_rule: Topics and scripts are original. Reference videos are used only for format and title patterns, never footage, characters, audio or text.

topics.title: What if friction disappeared for 5 seconds?
topics.hook: You're crossing a street in Chicago when friction switches off. Your shoes stop gripping. So does everything else.
beats: 0-3s title card + countdown HUD 'FRICTION RETURNS IN 0:05.000'
knots untie, shoelaces slide out, a parked car drifts downhill
nails and screws slide out of wood, a bookshelf comes apart
woven clothes unravel (threads only stay together by friction)
you can't stand: every step is ice, everyone slides to the lowest point
countdown hits 0: everything stops at once, wherever it ended up
real-fact card + 'Which force next?' CTA
topics.evidence: man_ia_c 'X disappeared for N seconds' formula: electrons 18.2M (29x median), oxygen 13.4M (21x), neutrons 5.1M (8x), pi=3 3.9M (6x), iron 2.7M (4x). Friction is not one of their topics.
topics.risk: Keep it playful, PG: no injuries shown in close-up.
topics.reuse_and_assets: new: side-view flat city street, sliding physics with easing; countdown HUD + serif caption are shared across all 'N seconds' shorts
facts_to_verify: fabric yarns are held together by friction between fibres

topics.title: What if calcium disappeared for 5 seconds?
topics.hook: Every skeleton on Earth just went soft. Including yours.
beats: title + countdown
X-ray view of you: bones turn rubbery (the vinegar chicken-bone trick, but everywhere)
you fold to the ground like a puppet
marble statues, limestone pyramids and chalk cliffs crumble to sand
concrete loses its binder: sidewalks turn to gravel
seashells and coral reefs dissolve in the sea
calcium returns: real-fact card (99% of your calcium is in bones and teeth)
topics.evidence: same formula as #1; man_ia_c's 'body' beats (blood turns grey in iron, 'you weigh as much as a 5-year-old' in neutrons) are their highest-share moments
topics.risk: Body-horror tone: keep stylised, not gory.
topics.reuse_and_assets: X-ray stick figure (new), ocean kit coral/shells (B3 reuse), simple building silhouettes
facts_to_verify: ~99% of body calcium is in bones and teeth

topics.title: What if you could breathe underwater?
topics.hook: You fall off a ferry in the middle of the Pacific, take a panicked breath... and nothing happens. You're fine.
beats: cold open: fall, gasp, calm
'here's how it works': water holds ~1/30 of the oxygen air does, so you need gills the size of a duvet
real science: liquid-breathing mice (1966)
dive ladder with depth meter: 10 m, 40 m, 100 m: pressure is the next problem
meet the neighbours: whale, squid, anglerfish (scale bars)
the cold, the dark, the bends you no longer get
your options list: where would you live?
payoff: the trench floor; 'next: what if you could see every colour?'
topics.evidence: IFOLOGY's classic power titles average 2-10x median (10x Faster 868K, Stop Time 636K, Shapeshift 436K); Depth Theory ocean explainer 2.28M on 6K subs (PLAN.md). Combines both proven demands.
topics.risk: None; good 9:16 cut-down.
topics.reuse_and_assets: Direct reuse of B3 explainer kit: depth gradient, creatures, depth meter, scale bar, YOU figure, options list
facts_to_verify: seawater dissolved O2 roughly 1/30 to 1/40 of air by volume

topics.title: What if light slowed to walking speed for 5 seconds?
topics.hook: Light now moves as fast as you walk. Everything you see is already in the past.
beats: title + countdown
your friend waving 10 m away: you see her 7 seconds late
walk toward a stop sign and it turns blue, walk away and it turns red
your phone screen is 'still loading' because the light is
the Sun keeps shining: the light already on its way is now crawling
light speed returns: 5 seconds of backlog hits your eyes at once
real fact: in 1999 a lab slowed light to 17 m/s
topics.evidence: formula as #1; 'pi was exactly 3' (3.9M) shows abstract physics-constant changes work, not just elements
topics.risk: Physics is hand-wavy; label it a thought experiment.
topics.reuse_and_assets: flat 2D park scene, colour-shift filter, delayed 'ghost' copies of characters (pure code)
facts_to_verify: Lene Hau 1999: light slowed to ~17 m/s in a Bose-Einstein condensate

topics.title: What if everyone on Earth was born on the same day?
topics.hook: 8 billion babies. One birthday. The hospitals have about nine months to get ready.
beats: cold open: every maternity ward, one morning
year 5: the world needs a billion school desks at once
year 18: everyone graduates, every job has 8 billion applicants
the population pyramid becomes a stick: chart animates
year 40: the midlife crisis, all at once
year 65: everyone retires, nobody is left to work
year 90: the long goodbye; who has kids, and when?
payoff: why age spread keeps a species alive
topics.evidence: Awaken's humanity-scale 'Can 2 People Really Restart Humanity?' 4.2M (23x median) is mostly flat 2D: chalkboard, population trees, timeline stamps ('YEAR 20', '+50 YEARS'). Same data-driven arc, original premise.
topics.risk: None.
topics.reuse_and_assets: explainer kit charts + new: timeline stamp, population pyramid, crowd of stick figures (instanced SVG)

topics.title: What if air became as thick as water for 5 seconds?
topics.hook: You take one step outside... and start floating.

you're neutrally buoyant: people drift off the sidewalk like divers
a 20 km/h breeze now hits like a flood current
birds swim, planes float like balloons
shouting sounds different: sound moves 4x faster
you can't breathe it in fast enough: lungs pumping syrup
air returns: everyone drops 2 metres

the deepest fish ever filmed (8,336 m)

your options list
payoff at the surface

what the world would look like if everyone stopped

topics.title: What if the Sun disappeared for 5 seconds?
topics.hook: The Sun just vanished. And for the next 8 minutes, nothing happens.
beats: title + countdown
nothing happens: light already on its way keeps arriving
gravity also travels at light speed: Earth keeps orbiting nothing
8 min 20 s later: 5 seconds of total darkness
stars appear at noon, temperature drop is tiny
the Sun is back. Real fact: 2017 neutron-star merger proved gravity moves at light speed
topics.evidence: man_ia_c 'Earth left the universe' (429K) and 'black hole' (650K) show space-scale topics are average; the anti-climax twist is the hook
topics.risk: Anti-climax could tank retention; test as a short only.
topics.reuse_and_assets: flat sky/space scene, orbit diagram, countdown HUD
facts_to_verify: sunlight takes ~8 min 20 s to reach Earth
